Let me analyze this specification. It's about Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d), Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s), Spring XD, and related module infrastructure. The user stories describe:

- U1: Enforce external libraries from overriding any existing library in the uber-jar (build tooling, maven shade/duplicate handling)
- U2: Move the external library to its own project (project restructuring, Maven multi-module)
- U3: Port SFTP module from Spring XD to spring-cloud-stream (s-c-s) repo as source module
- U4: Create a new project to contain all rules associated with @RedisRule contract, isolated from core, reusable by tests; possibly move to Spring Integration "commons"
- U5: Create foundation to support processor as OOTB (out-of-the-box) modules, using processor modules from s-c-s-m (spring-cloud-stream-modules) repo
- U6: Enable offline mode for AetherModuleResolver, pulling module artifacts from local maven repo
- U7: Create ModuleRegistry implementation to look up module coordinates by name
- U8: Create shell commands: module info, module list, module register, module unregister interacting with ModuleRegistry

This is essentially estimating work for the Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream Modules early development (circa 2015). These user stories look like they come from actual spring-cloud-dataflow / spring-cloud-stream-modules GitHub issues.

I need to produce a WBS-based estimate with activities, each with a most likely effort in work-hours, plus technical/design decisions and assumptions, and total.

3. U2: Move external library to its own project (repo setup, maven module extraction, refactor imports, CI)
4. U3: Port SFTP source module from XD to s-c-s repo (code port, adapt to new programming model, tests, docs)
5. U4: Create Redis test rules project (@RedisRule), extract from core, publish as test utility
6. U5: Foundation for processor OOTB modules (module framework, config, pom structure, sample processor)
7. U6: Offline mode for AetherModuleResolver
8. U7: ModuleRegistry implementation (interface + default impl, maybe Redis or in-memory? Actually in spring-cloud-dataflow, ModuleRegistry had a Redis-backed implementation initially)
9. U8: Shell commands module info/list/register/unregister
10. Integration testing and documentation
11. Build/CI setup

- Java 17+ with Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3 baseline per spec.
- Maven multi-module builds; Maven Shade Plugin (or Spring Boot thin launcher?) for uber-jar; enforce unique classes via maven-enforcer extra-enforcer-rules duplicateClasses or shade DuplicateClassesWarning... Actually the real solution in spring-cloud-stream-modules: "spring-cloud-stream-module-plugin" with "module plugin" to prevent overriding. Keep generic: use Maven Enforcer with extra rule / shade plugin config and a custom check.
- New Git project for external library with own release cycle.

- Existing repos and CI infrastructure exist; permissions available.

- The "external library" in U1/U2 refers to the existing uber-jar packaging library (e.g., module launcher/aggregator) in s-c-d repo.
- SFTP port includes source only (per story) not sink.

A10 "Cross-cutting integration and end-to-end testing" — wire registry + resolver + shell + modules together; end-to-end scenario tests; regression fixes. 32h.

technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline stack: Java 17+, Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, Maven multi-module builds, per the specification's Spring 6 / Java 17 requirement.

U1: Enforce no-override of existing classes in the uber-jar at build time using Maven Enforcer (duplicate classes rule) plus strict Maven Shade plugin configuration so the build fails when an external library repackages/overrides existing classes; add an automated verification test that intentionally introduces a duplicate and asserts build failure.
U2: Extract the external (uber-jar packaging/launching) library into its own Git/Maven project with independent groupId/artifactId/version and release cycle; s-c-d consumes it as a normal dependency.

U3: Port the XD SFTP module as a Spring Cloud Stream source module using @EnableBinding(Source.class), Spring Integration SFTP inbound channel adapters, and @ConfigurationProperties for options; integration tests run against an embedded Apache MINA SSHD SFTP server.

U4: Implement @RedisRule support as a standalone test-support artifact (JUnit rule/extension, e.g., RedisAvailableRule) in a new project, published as a reusable dependency; core modules migrate their tests to it. Structure the code so it can later be donated to Spring Integration 'commons'.

U5: Define a processor module foundation: a parent POM/module template in the s-c-s-m repo, conventions based on the Spring Cloud Stream Processor binding, configuration-metadata generation, and a minimal sample processor to validate the foundation.

U6: Implement offline mode in AetherModuleResolver via Maven Resolver (Aether) configuration: an 'offline' flag that disables remote repositories and resolves artifacts solely from the local Maven repository, with clear error reporting when an artifact is absent locally.

U7: Define a ModuleRegistry API (lookup by name, list, register, unregister of module coordinates including type: source/processor/sink) with a default persistent implementation, plus an in-memory implementation for tests.

U8: Implement shell commands (module list, module info, module register, module unregister) with a Spring Shell-based command layer delegating to the ModuleRegistry, including argument validation and tabular output formatting.
Unit tests are included within each implementation activity; a separate activity covers cross-cutting integration/end-to-end testing across registry, resolver, shell, and modules.
assumptions: A single experienced Spring/Java developer performs all work; estimates are effort (work-hours), not elapsed time.
Existing repositories, build infrastructure, and CI are available and the developer has required permissions; only new-project CI wiring is in scope.

Estimates include design, implementation, unit tests, and activity-level integration tests, plus developer self-review; they exclude project management, formal QA cycles, release management, and deployment to production.
The 'external library' in U1/U2 is the existing uber-jar packaging/launching library currently embedded in the s-c-d repository.
U3 covers porting the SFTP source module only (no sink), as stated in the story.

U4 requires one default persistent ModuleRegistry backing store (e.g., Redis-backed or embedded store) plus an in-memory variant for tests; migration to SI 'commons' is only prepared for, not executed.
U8 interaction is shell-based only; no web UI changes are required.
Where specification details are missing (e.g., exact module metadata format, storage technology), reasonable standard choices are made and are covered by the listed activities without extra scope.
